description: Searches local business listings near a coordinate. Use this to find local business candidates or nearby competitors; it does not run Maps rank checks or Q&A. CHARGES CREDITS ONLY WHEN APIFY IS CONFIGURED AND ITS SHARED MONTHLY BUDGET HAS ROOM: results then come from a real, independently-run scrape of Google Places (`dataSource: "apify_google_places"`) — real ratings, since OpenStreetMap never has one. Otherwise (Apify unconfigured, over budget, or the actor call failed) NOTHING IS CHARGED and this falls back automatically to OpenStreetMap (Overpass, then Nominatim) — real point-of-interest data, no key (`dataSource: "openstreetmap"`) — whose coverage is uneven and carries none of a commercial directory's ranking, review or category metadata. Do not present an OpenStreetMap result set as the complete set of businesses in the area; the response's own `dataSource` field on each row says which source actually answered it, never assume. `categories` values are common category names (e.g. 'restaurant', 'dentist'); OpenStreetMap matches them on a best-effort basis, so a category that returns nothing on that path may simply be unmapped there rather than absent from the area — an empty result is not measured coverage of the area, and a listing's missing rating or review count is likewise not measured, never zero.

limit.description: Maximum businesses to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

near.description: Coordinate and radius to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the center, in kilometers. get_google_business_questions clamps it to roughly 0.2-200 km and ignores it entirely on the free provider — see that tool's description before reporting a radius as applied.

projectId.description: Required. The MisarSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

query.description: Business name or title text to match.

name: search_local_businesses
